title: Prime Medicine Wins Arbitration Against Beam Therapeutics Over AATD Gene-Editing Candidate
detail: Prime Medicine announced a positive, binding resolution of its arbitration with Beam Therapeutics concerning their 2019 collaboration and license agreement. The tribunal ruled Prime Medicine owes no monetary damages and declared that PM647 — a prime-editing candidate for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) that corrects the E342K (Pi*Z) mutation in SERPINA1 using Prime's universal liver LNP — falls within Prime Medicine's contractual 'Field,' confirming its right to develop and commercialize the program. Prime Medicine plans to submit an IND/CTA filing for PM647 in Q3 2026, with initial clinical data expected in 2027, potentially putting it in direct competition with Beam's own AATD base-editing program (BEAM-302).

media.caption: Prime Medicine wins binding arbitration against Beam Therapeutics over PM647

title: Allotera Therapeutics (formerly Wugen) Raises $35M to Advance CRISPR-Edited Off-the-Shelf CAR-T
detail: Allotera Therapeutics — rebranded from Wugen — closed a $35 million extension of its Series C financing (bringing the round total to $150 million), primarily to support the ongoing global pivotal T-RRex trial of soficabtagene geleucel (sofi-cel), an allogeneic, healthy-donor-derived CAR-T therapy that uses CRISPR-Cas9 to delete CD7 and TRAC for relapsed or refractory T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia and T-cell lymphoblastic lymphoma. Sofi-cel holds FDA Breakthrough Therapy, RMAT, Fast Track, Orphan Drug, and Rare Pediatric Disease designations, plus EU PRIME designation.

media.caption: Allotera Therapeutics raises $35M to advance CRISPR-edited CAR-T for T-cell cancers
